text_to_speech.example2: A spoken version of a weekly summary
text_to_speech.needs: An API key for the speech provider in the vault. Each clip is billed by that provider, per character.
text_to_speech.never: Never sends audio anywhere; the clip appears in the conversation.

video_generation.name: Video generation
video_generation.does: Makes a short video from a description, or from an image it starts with.
video_generation.example1: A ten-second teaser for a product launch
video_generation.example2: An animated version of a generated logo
video_generation.needs: An API key for the video provider in the vault. Each clip is billed by that provider, per second.
video_generation.never: Never posts a video anywhere; it appears in the conversation.

knowledge.name: Knowledge search
knowledge.does: Lets the agent answer from your documents and say which one each answer came from.
knowledge.example1: Answer staff questions from the HR handbook
knowledge.example2: Find the termination clause in the contracts
knowledge.needs: A knowledge base with documents, picked in this panel.
knowledge.never: Never searches a knowledge base this agent is not connected to.

media.name: Media offload
media.does: Moves images out of a long conversation's history, so it stays small and cheaper to send.

memory_files.name: Memory
memory_files.does: Lets the agent keep notes from one conversation to the next, so it does not start from zero.
memory_files.example1: Remember somebody's team and what they work on
memory_files.example2: Keep a running list of open questions
memory_files.never: Never shows one person's notes to another. In a group chat the notes belong to the chat.

memory_mem0.name: Memory (mem0)
memory_mem0.does: Lets the agent remember facts and recall them by meaning, stored in a mem0 service.
memory_mem0.example1: Remember that a customer prefers email to phone calls
memory_mem0.needs: A mem0 account, cloud or self-hosted, and its API key in the vault.
memory_mem0.never: Never shows one person's memories to another. In a group chat they belong to the chat.

planning.name: Planning
planning.does: Lets the agent write a checklist for a bigger task and tick off each step, so the person sees its progress.
planning.example1: Prepare a monthly report in five visible steps
planning.never: Never gives the agent permission to do anything; a plan is only a list.

background_tools.name: Work while tools run
background_tools.does: Lets the agent start a slow tool - a long browse - and carry on with the rest of the request, using the result when it arrives.
background_tools.example1: Check three suppliers' portals and draft the email while the browses run
background_tools.needs: A capability with a slow tool, such as the web browser.
background_tools.never: Never runs anything after the run ends; stopping the run stops its background tools.

sandbox.name: Sandbox
sandbox.does: Gives the agent its own small computer: it creates and edits files and runs code, and the files are still there next time.
sandbox.example1: Clean up a spreadsheet and hand back the result
sandbox.example2: Write a script, run it and fix it until it works
sandbox.example3: Keep a draft report it updates over several days
sandbox.needs: A sandbox. A standard deployment sets one up on its own; otherwise an administrator adds one under Sandboxes.
sandbox.never: Never reaches your computer or other company systems. Changing files and running commands wait for a person's approval, unless you change that.

skills.name: Skills
skills.does: Lets the agent follow your written how-tos, loading one when the task needs it.
skills.example1: Write a proposal the way your sales team does
skills.example2: Follow the checklist for a new client
skills.needs: Skills, written under Skills and picked in this panel.
skills.never: Never changes a skill; the agent only reads it.

subagents.name: Subagents
subagents.does: Lets the agent hand part of a job to another agent and use its answer.
subagents.example1: A front-desk agent that passes legal questions to the legal agent
subagents.example2: Research several topics side by side
subagents.needs: Other agents, or specialists defined in this panel. Each handover costs what that agent's run costs.
subagents.never: Never gives another agent more access than it already has.

system_reminders.name: Instruction reminders
system_reminders.does: Repeats the agent's key instructions during a long task, so it does not drift away from them.
system_reminders.example1: A long research task that has to keep the requested format
system_reminders.never: Adds no tools; it only repeats the instructions.

thinking.name: Thinking
thinking.does: Lets the model think before it answers - slower and more expensive, but better on problems with several steps.
thinking.example1: Compare three versions of a contract
thinking.example2: Work out a schedule with many constraints
thinking.never: Adds no tools; it changes how the model answers.

tool_output_limits.name: Tool output limits
tool_output_limits.does: Shortens a very large tool result, so it is not sent to the model again with every message.
tool_output_limits.example1: A search that returns a huge spreadsheet
tool_output_limits.never: Never changes the data itself, only how much of it the model reads at once.

tool_search.name: Tool search
tool_search.does: Lets an agent with many tools find the right one when it needs it, instead of reading all of them every time.
tool_search.example1: An agent connected to several MCP servers with dozens of tools
tool_search.never: Never adds a tool; it only hides tools until the agent looks for one.

web_fetch.name: Read web pages
web_fetch.does: Lets the agent open a link and read the page.
web_fetch.never: Never logs in or fills in a form; it only reads.

web_research.name: Web search
web_research.does: Lets the agent search the internet for current information.
web_research.example1: What changed in this regulation this year?
web_research.example2: Find three competitors and their prices
web_research.needs: Nothing, with DuckDuckGo. Brave, Exa or Tavily need their API key in the vault.
web_research.never: Never sends your documents to the search engine, only the search words.

visuals.name: Visuals
visuals.does: Draws in the conversation - a diagram, an architecture map, an explainer with sliders, a 3D scene - live while the agent writes it. A drawing can be saved as an app.
visuals.example1: Our order flow as a diagram
visuals.example2: A 3D model of the warehouse you can turn
visuals.needs: Nothing extra. The visual-design skill makes the drawings look designed.
visuals.never: Never reaches the network - a drawing runs sealed off, like an app's page.

follow_ups.name: Follow-ups
follow_ups.does: Offers up to three next steps as buttons under an answer, so what to ask next is one click away.
follow_ups.needs: Nothing extra. The buttons show in the web chat, the widget and the hosted page.
follow_ups.never: Never sends anything on its own - a step goes out only when someone clicks it.

audience.label: Who can use it
audience.onlyMeHint: You, and whoever you share it with later.
audience.noGroupsYet: No groups yet - add them under Groups, or type to find a person.
audience.chosenHint: Only the departments and people you pick.
audience.chooseAudience: Groups and people who can use it
audience.noMatches: Nothing matches - try a name or an email address.
audience.typeForPeople: Type a name or an email address to find a person.

cdp_url.title: DevTools endpoint
cdp_url.description: Chromium DevTools endpoint to drive - a browser service the operator runs, not a process in the API container.

allowed_domains.title: Allowed domains
allowed_domains.description: Hosts the browser may be on; empty means no restriction. Globs like *.example.com are allowed. Checked on every step, not only the first.

max_steps.title: Steps per call at most
max_steps.description: How many steps one call may take; each step is one model request. A task that needs more continues in the same tab on the next call.

vision.title: Show the model screenshots
vision.description: Send each step's screenshot to the model as well as the page's elements. Better on visual pages, more tokens, and the model has to read images.

candidate_cap.title: Elements offered per step
candidate_cap.description: How many of the page's elements may be offered as choices in one step. Lower is cheaper and blinder; the answer to a page too dense for the cap is to scroll.

preview.title: Show a live preview
preview.description: Send the viewport to the chat while the browse runs, so a person can watch it. Costs one JPEG per step on the socket.

preview_width.title: Viewport width (pixels)
preview_width.description: The browser's viewport width in pixels, which is also how wide the frames are. It decides what the agent can see without scrolling.

step_model_profile_id.title: Model for each browse step
step_model_profile_id.description: A model profile `browse_web` asks for each step instead of the agent's own. Steps are most of a browse's time and cost, so a cheaper model here makes a long browse cheaper, and quicker where its provider answers quickly - measure it, since a small model through a slow gateway is no faster. Empty uses the agent's model. The agent's own browser tools always use it.

connection.title: How the browser reaches the web
connection.description: Built in uses the deployment's browser and its address. A proxy sends the browses through an address of your own - a residential or regional one sites block less. A hosted browser runs them in a browser service you pay for, reached over CDP.

proxy_url.title: Proxy address
proxy_url.description: http://, https:// or socks5:// with the host and port. Its username:password goes in the vault, picked below; Chromium cannot sign in to a SOCKS proxy.

hosted_url.title: Hosted browser address
hosted_url.description: The service's wss:// CDP address. Its key goes in the vault, picked below, and is added to the address's query when the browse connects.

hosted_key_param.title: Query parameter for the key
hosted_key_param.description: What the hosted browser calls its key in the address's query.

timezone.title: Time zone the browser reports
timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as Europe/Warsaw. Set it to match the proxy's region: a browser whose clock and address disagree reads as a bot.

locale.title: Language the browser reports
locale.description: A language tag such as pl-PL, sent as Accept-Language and navigator.language.

tools.title: Allowed lookups
tools.description: Which channel lookups this binding allows, by tool id. Empty means none, which is what a binding starts as.

default_limit.title: Results when no number is asked for
default_limit.description: Members, search results or messages returned when the model does not ask for a number

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the agent thinks in, e.g. Europe/Warsaw

timeout_secs.title: Time limit per call (seconds)
timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock budget for one call, in seconds

max_memory_mb.title: Memory limit per call (MB)
max_memory_mb.description: Memory cap for one call, in megabytes

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.description: Which strategy to apply when the history approaches the window

max_fraction.title: Start at this share of the window
max_fraction.description: Fraction of the model's context window at which compaction starts

keep_messages.title: Recent messages kept
keep_messages.description: How many recent messages survive a summary or a sliding window

keep_tool_pairs.title: Recent tool results kept
keep_tool_pairs.description: How many recent tool calls keep their results when results are cleared

summary_prompt.title: Summary prompt
summary_prompt.description: What the summarising model is told. `{messages}` is where the conversation being replaced is inserted, and it is required - a prompt without it summarises nothing. Edit it to keep what your agent's work depends on: the default keeps intent, decisions and open threads, which is not the same as what a support transcript or a code review needs

context_window.title: Context window override
context_window.description: Override the window this triggers against. Also what the chat's context gauge divides by, so the two describe one ceiling. Set it when the resolved number is wrong for your deployment - a beta or a tier can be given less than the provider publishes - or to make an agent compact earlier than its model would require

fallback_context_window.title: Fallback context window
fallback_context_window.description: Window to assume when the model's own cannot be resolved

expose_read_tool.title: Let the agent open linked files
expose_read_tool.description: Whether link-mode files are reachable through a read tool. Off means only injected files reach the model, and nothing is read on demand.

max_results.title: Conversations per search
max_results.description: How many conversations one search returns at most. Each brings back a short passage, so a high number costs context on every search.

redact_secrets_in.title: Hide secrets in the question
redact_secrets_in.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the user's prompt

redact_pii_in.title: Hide personal data in the question
redact_pii_in.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from the prompt

blocked_keywords_in.title: Blocked words in the question
blocked_keywords_in.description: Block the run if the prompt contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_out.title: Hide secrets in the answer
redact_secrets_out.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the agent's answer

redact_pii_out.title: Hide personal data in the answer
redact_pii_out.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from the answer

blocked_keywords_out.title: Blocked words in the answer
blocked_keywords_out.description: Block the run if the answer contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_tool.title: Hide secrets in tool results
redact_secrets_tool.description: Redact API keys and tokens from tool results before the model reads them

redact_pii_tool.title: Hide personal data in tool results
redact_pii_tool.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from tool results

blocked_keywords_tool.title: Blocked words in tool results
blocked_keywords_tool.description: Block the run if a tool result contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_args.title: Hide secrets in tool arguments
redact_secrets_args.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the arguments the agent passes a tool

redact_pii_args.title: Hide personal data in tool arguments
redact_pii_args.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from tool arguments

blocked_keywords_args.title: Blocked words in tool arguments
blocked_keywords_args.description: Block the run if a tool's arguments contain any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

phone_regions.title: Phone number countries
phone_regions.description: Countries whose national phone formats PII redaction reads, as two-letter codes (comma or newline separated), at most 16 regions and 256 characters. A number written with + is redacted whatever is listed

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose model draws. Only providers whose model class honours the image tool are accepted - three today - and which those are is asked of the SDK rather than listed here.

model.title: Image model
model.description: Which of that provider's image models draws, by the ids in `app/core/catalog/image_models.json`. A model outside the catalog is refused: the tool answers a model that cannot draw with an error its author only sees mid-run.

quality.title: Quality
quality.description: Rendering quality; higher is slower and dearer.

size.title: Size
size.description: Output size. OpenAI uses the pixel values, Google the K values.

background.title: Background
background.description: Background type; transparent needs a png or webp output.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose voices speak. Offered: the providers in `app/core/catalog/text_to_speech_models.json` whose key the vault can hold.

model.title: Speech model
model.description: Which of that provider's speech models speaks. A model outside the catalog is refused here rather than mid-run.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: The voice that speaks unless the agent chooses another; left empty, the model's first. ElevenLabs voices belong to your account, so for ElevenLabs paste the voice id from your voice library.

voices.title: Allowed voices
voices.description: The only voices the agent may switch to instead of the one above, per clip - for a dialogue, or a narrator and a character. Left empty, it may choose any voice the model offers - for ElevenLabs, any voice id in your account.

output_format.title: File format
output_format.description: mp3 is smaller, wav is uncompressed. Left empty, the provider's first format - Gemini returns wav only.

max_characters.title: Longest text
max_characters.description: The most text one call may speak, which caps what a single call can cost.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose model makes the video. Offered: the providers in `app/core/catalog/video_models.json` whose key the vault can hold.

model.title: Video model
model.description: Which of that provider's video models makes the clip. A model outside the catalog is refused here rather than mid-run.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: The resolution a clip is made at unless the agent asks for another; left empty, the model's first. Higher costs more per second.

max_resolution.title: Highest resolution
max_resolution.description: The highest resolution the agent may ask for, at least the usual one; it caps what a second can cost. Left empty, the agent may ask for any resolution the model renders.

aspect_ratio.title: Aspect ratio
aspect_ratio.description: The shape a clip takes unless the agent asks for another; left empty, the model's first.

seconds.title: Length
seconds.description: Seconds a clip runs unless the agent asks for another length; left empty, five, or the nearest the model makes. Not for a model that decides its own length.

max_seconds.title: Longest clip
max_seconds.description: The longest clip the agent may ask for, which caps what one call can cost; left empty, the model's own limit. Not for a model that decides its own length.

audio.title: Sound
audio.description: Whether clips carry sound unless the agent asks otherwise, where the model makes it optional; left empty, the provider's default.

alibaba_workspace.title: Alibaba workspace
alibaba_workspace.description: Alibaba only: the Model Studio workspace id, which Wan 3.0 is called through. Left empty, the shared DashScope endpoint, which Alibaba keeps for existing integrations.

alibaba_region.title: Alibaba region
alibaba_region.description: Alibaba only: the region the workspace is in.

timeout_seconds.title: Time limit
timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for a clip, in seconds. A job not finished by then is cancelled where the provider allows it and booked at its estimate.

default_top_k.title: Passages per search
default_top_k.description: Passages returned when the model does not ask for a number

self_query_enabled.title: Infer filters from the question
self_query_enabled.description: Infer FA-039 business filters (source, document type, organizational unit, date range) from the natural-language query with an LLM when the model searches without naming any filter itself. Off by default. Each such search makes one extra model request, billed to the run. It can only narrow within the agent's tenant and collections, never widen.

query_analysis_mode.title: Query expansion
query_analysis_mode.description: Optionally analyse and expand the query before retrieval to improve recall on short or fuzzy questions. Off by default. `multi_query` and `hyde` each make one extra model call

query_analysis_max_variants.title: Rephrasings at most
query_analysis_max_variants.description: How many rephrasings `multi_query` may add, bounding its fan-out and cost. Ignored by the other modes

parent_context.title: Include the surrounding text
parent_context.description: Small-to-big retrieval: return each matched chunk with the text around it. Matching and ranking always run on the small chunks, the matched chunk is never shortened, and the added context is bounded.

threshold_bytes.title: Store parts larger than (bytes)
threshold_bytes.description: Binary or text parts at least this large are written to storage and replaced with a reference in the stored history.

allow_personal.title: Keep private notes per person
allow_personal.description: Whether the agent keeps private notes for each person it talks to, readable only when it is alone with them. Off drops that store entirely, for compliance or privacy; the notes it keeps in group chats stay.

base_url.title: Self-hosted mem0 URL
base_url.description: Base URL of a self-hosted mem0; omit for mem0's managed cloud.

allow_personal.title: Keep private memories per person
allow_personal.description: Whether the agent keeps private memories for each person it talks to, readable only when it is alone with them. Off drops that store, for compliance or privacy; group-chat memory stays.

enable_subtasks.title: Subtasks and dependencies
enable_subtasks.description: Adds subtasks and dependencies: a step waits as blocked until the steps before it finish. Off by default, because a flat checklist is enough for most work.

cache_ttl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
cache_ttl.description: How long the provider may cache the prompt prefix that sits before the plan reminder. The reminder changes every turn and is deliberately kept behind this breakpoint so the stable prefix stays cacheable; a longer TTL suits a conversation that stays open, the shorter one a burst of turns.

backend.title: Where files live
backend.description: state: files only, no shell, stored by the platform - works on every deployment with no extra services. service: a container or cloud sandbox, on one of the connections this organization has registered.

connection_id.title: Sandbox connection
connection_id.description: Which registered sandbox connection to run on; empty takes the organization's default. An id, never an address or a token - a spec is exported to a client's git repository, so the only thing it may carry is a reference. The connection decides whether that is a container on a host you run or a sandbox in Daytona's cloud.

session_scope.title: Who shares the workspace
session_scope.description: Who shares one workspace: run (a fresh one every turn), conversation (everyone in the chat or Slack thread), channel (a whole Slack channel), user (one person across chats) or agent (everyone who talks to it).

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.description: Which environment a container-backed workspace runs, named from the list the connection's service allows. Empty takes the connection's default. An alias, never an image.

include_execute.title: Allow shell commands
include_execute.description: Whether the agent may run shell commands. Turning it off leaves the file tools and removes the shell entirely, rather than gating it.

inline.title: Inline specialists
inline.description: Specialists defined inside this agent, for work that does not justify publishing an agent of its own. Not versioned: editing this agent changes them, and nothing else can reference them.

mode.title: Delegation mode
mode.description: Sync waits for the delegate's answer, async collects it later, auto lets the model choose per task. A background delegation cannot wait for an approval, so keep work that needs one on sync.

allow_questions.title: Let delegates ask questions
allow_questions.description: Lets a delegate ask the person waiting a question instead of guessing. Works only for a sync delegation, and only for the specialists this agent was given. A question is not an approval and cannot grant one.

allow_dynamic.title: Let the agent create specialists
allow_dynamic.description: Lets this agent write its own specialists while it runs. Each is instructions and one of your models, with no tools or knowledge, spends from this run's budget and is gone after the reply. Gate `create_agent` to see each one first.

max_depth.title: Delegation depth
max_depth.description: How many levels of delegation are allowed, counting this agent. 1 lets it delegate but not its delegates; 2 allows one nested level. Each level multiplies the requests one turn can make.

max_fanout.title: Delegations at once
max_fanout.description: How many delegations may run at once. Reached, the next one is refused with a message the model can act on rather than an error. This is the ceiling on a background delegation launching a background delegation until a dozen agents are running against one budget.

max_result_chars.title: Answer length shown per delegate
max_result_chars.description: How much of a finished delegation's answer is shown when several are collected at once. A truncated one says so and points at the tool that returns it in full, so nothing is lost - this only decides how much of five specialists' work arrives in one turn's context.

share_with_delegates.title: Capabilities delegates inherit
share_with_delegates.description: Capabilities this agent passes on to its delegates, such as a shared workspace so one writes a file and another reads it. Nothing is shared unless named here, and delegation itself never is.

reminders.title: Fixed reminders
reminders.description: Fixed lines re-stated on their own cadences

goal_reanchor.title: Restate the original request
goal_reanchor.description: Re-state the original request on a cadence, at no token cost

llm_reminder.title: Model-written reminder
llm_reminder.description: A model-written reminder on a cadence. Costs one extra call each fire

cache_ttl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
cache_ttl.description: Cache lifetime of the breakpoint placed before the tail reminder

effort.title: Reasoning effort
effort.description: How hard the model reasons before answering. Leave unset for the provider's own default effort; a level a provider does not have maps to its closest one.

action.title: When a result is too long
action.description: What to do with a return once it is over the threshold

threshold.title: Size limit
threshold.description: Size at or above which a return is reduced. Characters by default; estimated tokens when 'over tokens' is set, where it defaults to 15,000

over_tokens.title: Measure in tokens
over_tokens.description: Measure the threshold in estimated tokens rather than characters

max_chars.title: Characters kept
max_chars.description: Characters kept when a return is truncated, or when a spill or summary falls back to truncation. Left unset, never more than the threshold

truncation_strategy.title: Which part to keep
truncation_strategy.description: Which end(s) of an oversized text to keep when truncating

strip_ansi.title: Strip terminal colours
strip_ansi.description: Strip terminal colour codes from text returns before measuring and reducing

summary_prompt.title: Summary prompt
summary_prompt.description: What the summarising model is told, for the 'summarize' action. Must contain {output}, where the tool's full output is inserted; {tool_name} is available too, for the name of the tool that produced it

strategy.title: Search method
strategy.description: auto: native tool search on a provider that supports it, local keyword matching elsewhere. keywords: always match locally, on any provider. bm25 / regex: force an Anthropic-native algorithm; errors on a provider that has no native tool search.

max_results.title: Matches per search
max_results.description: How many matches the local search returns; ignored for native search.

method.title: How pages are fetched
method.description: local: we fetch the page, identically on every model. native: the model provider fetches it with its own egress and citations (only on models that support it). auto: native where the model has it, ours everywhere else.

max_content_chars.title: Page length limit (characters)
max_content_chars.description: How much of a page one fetch returns before it is truncated; roughly four characters per token. Ignored under native fetch, which the provider bounds itself.

allowed_domains.title: Allowed domains
allowed_domains.description: Bare hostnames the agent may fetch, e.g. docs.example.com; empty means any. Matched exactly - no wildcards, no subdomains.

blocked_domains.title: Blocked domains
blocked_domains.description: Bare hostnames the agent may never fetch, matched exactly.

method.title: Search engine
method.description: duckduckgo: free, no account, results rendered as clickable sources. native: the model provider searches with its own index and citations (only on models that support it). tavily: summarised for a model to read. brave: an index of its own. exa: search by meaning rather than keywords.

max_results.title: Results per search
max_results.description: How many results one search returns; ignored for native search.

harness.title: Coding agent
harness.description: Which coding agent does the work: Claude Code, on an Anthropic key or a Claude subscription token, or Codex, on an OpenAI key or a ChatGPT sign-in.

access.title: What it may do
access.description: Change files and run commands, such as tests - or only read the code and answer. Set Human approval to ask before each task either way.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model the coding agent runs: a Claude model for Claude Code, an OpenAI one for Codex. Not set takes the coding agent's own default.

base_url.title: Anthropic-compatible endpoint
base_url.description: Claude Code only: a gateway that speaks Anthropic's API, such as https://openrouter.ai/api, with the key in the vault being that gateway's. Empty calls Anthropic directly.

timeout_minutes.title: Time limit (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: How long one task may run before it is stopped.

model_profile_id.title: Model for next steps
model_profile_id.description: A model profile that writes the next steps once the answer is in, instead of the agent's own model offering them as a tool. A small, cheap model is enough for three short buttons, and the agent no longer spends a request on them. Empty lets the agent offer them itself.

apiReference.title: API reference
apiReference.description: Every endpoint an API key can call on this deployment (version {version}), read from its own OpenAPI document. Open an endpoint for its parameters, body, responses and a ready curl call.
apiReference.authBody: Send the key in the Authorization: Bearer aos_… header. It acts in the organization it was issued in, with the permissions it was issued with and never more than its issuer holds now, and it is rate limited on its own.
apiReference.name: Name
apiReference.loadError: The API reference could not be loaded.

mcpConnect.title: Connect an MCP client
mcpConnect.why: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other MCP client can work in this organization through AgenticOS's own MCP server: list and run agents, read runs and what they cost, search and fill knowledge bases, invite members.
mcpConnect.docs: What the MCP server can do
mcpConnect.browserHint: The client opens this console, you choose the organization and what it may do, and its access renews itself. Connected clients are listed below.
mcpConnect.keyHint: For a client that cannot open a browser. Create a key above and set it as AGENTICOS_API_KEY in the client’s environment.

claude-code.browser: Run this, then type /mcp in Claude Code and choose agenticos to sign in.
claude-code.key: Run this with AGENTICOS_API_KEY set in your shell.

codex.browser: The second command opens the browser to sign in.
